answer: Shared-beacon drift fingerprinting. Each identity must periodically report a signed reading of a rotating public beacon; agents also wander across regions, leaving a pigment of timestamped location traces. A clone reusing one identity's key reveals itself when two readings for the same beacon epoch diverge beyond clock skew, or when traces overlap impossibly. Enforcing this costs an attacker a separate live host, clock, and trace history per clone, so duplication multiplies real infrastructure rather than keys.
